To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the heat exchanger effectiveness depends on the NTU and fluid-capacity ratio along with six quantities that represent the magnitude and axial variations of the heat leak and kinetic energy on the cold and hot sides of the heat-exchanger.
in the presence of significant heat leak and variation of kinetic energy, the effectiveness of a parallel-flow heat exchanger depends on NTU and capacity ratio along with five other quantities.
the closed-form expressions for effectiveness in the presence of axial variation in kinetic energy and heat leaks are given as E=1-(1-(1-NTU)(1-CR)exp(-NTU*F))/F, where F=1+CR+2*CR*F1+CR*F2+CR*F1*F2.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new methodology for heat exchanger design, which is based on the effectiveness-NTU method and is applicable for the case of heat exchangers having fluids with significant variation in the velocity.
the effect of kinetic energy and heat leaks on the effectiveness of parallel-flow heat exchanger.
the development of the effectiveness-NTU relation for parallel-flow heat transfer in heat exchangers in the presence of axial variations in kinetic energy and heat transfer from outside.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effectiveness of parallel-flow heat exchanger with fluids having significant kinetic energy variation and/or heat leak from outside, depends on NTU, fluid capacity ratio and the six other quantities that represent the kinetic energy and the heat leak.

the kinetic energy variation has a profound impact on the effectiveness of the heat transfer in the heat exchanger and the heat leak has a significant effect on the effectiveness of parallel-flow heat exchanger.
the effectiveness of a parallel-flow heat exchanger depends on NTU, fluid capacity ratio along, with the magnitude and axial distributions of kinetic energy and heat leaks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effectiveness of the parallel flow heat exchanger depends not only on the heat transfer area and the heat capacities of the fluids but also on the kinetic energy of the fluids and the heat leakage from the environment.
for a given heat exchanger configuration, the effectiveness-NTU relation depends on the kinetic energy and the heat leak on both hot and cold sides.
the effectiveness-NTU relation is not a function of the NTU alone, as commonly believed, and that it depends on several parameters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the heat exchanger effectiveness depends on the magnitude and distribution of the kinetic energies of the fluids and heat leak on both sides of the heat transfer surface.
the effectiveness of the parallel-flow heat exchanger depends on the axial distribution of the fluid kinetic energy and heat leakage on the hot and/or cold sides of the exchanger.
in the case of parallel-flow heat exchanger, the effectiveness-NTU relation depends only on the heat capacity ratio and the NTU.
